directions.name: Tile and Courtyard
directions.summary: Cobalt and turquoise glaze, as in glazed tilework.
directions.curation: Turquoise and cobalt glazes are documented in Persian, Central Asian and Ottoman tilework. This is one regional tradition, so it fits best where a community recognizes it.

reasoning.claim: Turquoise Glaze reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Cobalt, so either color can carry text on the other.
Turquoise and cobalt glazes appear in Persian and Ottoman tilework. Scholarship cautions against fixed symbolic readings, so the pair references craft and place rather than a meaning.

use_for: Institutions with a connection to this craft tradition
directions.watch_out: This references a specific regional tradition. Confirm it fits the community before using it.
directions.choose_if: the community recognises Persian, Central Asian or Ottoman tile traditions
do: Use the pair in pattern and large fields.

directions.name: Chalk and Slate
directions.summary: A slate ground with chalk-white type: the classroom board.
directions.curation: Taken from the classroom board: a muted dark ground and a chalk figure, calm enough for long reading.

reasoning.claim: Chalk reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Slate, so the dark ground carries all text.
A board-like pair reads as learning without the primary colors of children's education.

directions.watch_out: Dark grounds are harder for long documents. Provide a light variant for printouts.
directions.choose_if: an educational institution wants a calm, board-like identity without primary colors
do: Use Chalk for all text and diagrams.
avoid: Do not add bright primary colors.

directions.name: Afterhours
directions.summary: A violet-black with a hot magenta.
directions.curation: A night-time identity with one saturated color doing the work of stage lighting.

reasoning.claim: Hot Magenta reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Club Black, enough for graphics and headlines.
A saturated magenta on black feels electric and nocturnal.

directions.watch_out: Magenta is a common nightlife shorthand. The specificity has to come from type and imagery.
directions.choose_if: a club, venue or music brand lives at night and needs one electric color
do: Use Hot Magenta for headlines and the mark.

directions.name: Arcade Split
directions.summary: Deep blue against arcade orange: complementary and loud.
directions.curation: A complementary two-tone for games and entertainment, where both colors share the identity.

reasoning.claim: Arcade Orange reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Deep Blue, so it can carry type.
Near-complementary hues create energy and work well in characters and key art.

directions.watch_out: Complementary pairs vibrate at their edge. Avoid thin orange type on blue.
directions.choose_if: a game or entertainment brand wants two loud complementary colors in key art
do: Use bold type and large shapes.
avoid: Do not use thin orange text on blue.

directions.name: Festival Primaries
directions.summary: Sun yellow, primary blue and a red third color, in large blocks.
directions.curation: A primary-color system built as flat blocks, for events and products where joy matters more than restraint.

reasoning.claim: Primary Blue reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Sun, so type can sit on the yellow field.
Three chromatic colors each hold a substantial share of area, which makes this a Multicolor direction.

directions.watch_out: Three primaries can look childish. Precise layout and type keep it designed.
directions.choose_if: an event or children's product wants joyful flat color blocks
do: Assign one color to each kind of information.
avoid: Do not add gradients between the blocks.

directions.name: Story Night
directions.summary: Deep indigo with a moon yellow, for bedtime and story products.
directions.curation: A narrative pair: the night sky and the moon, for products about stories and sleep.

reasoning.claim: Moon Yellow reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Story Night in both directions.
A night scene gives the color a story-based reason, which suits bedtime ranges but not every children's product.

directions.watch_out: This is specific to night and sleep. It suits daytime ranges poorly.
directions.choose_if: the product is about stories, bedtime or sleep
do: Use Moon Yellow for the main character and the mark.
avoid: Do not add more bright colors.

directions.name: Newsprint Red
directions.summary: Newsprint and black with a single press red.
directions.curation: The newspaper: black type on off-white paper, with one red for what matters most.

reasoning.claim: Print Black reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Newsprint, so long reading is comfortable.
Press Red holds 3% of the declared area, so it keeps its emphasis.

directions.watch_out: Red also reads as error in interfaces. Define a separate error color.
directions.choose_if: reading is the main activity and one red should mark what matters
do: Use Press Red for one emphasis per page.
avoid: Do not use red for decoration.

directions.name: Museum Night
directions.summary: A dark gallery black with a cool cyan light.
directions.curation: A dark viewing room for media and collections, with one cool light color for navigation.

reasoning.claim: Gallery Cyan reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Gallery Black, so it can carry navigation and titles.
A dark ground lets images and film glow, and a single cool light reads as calm and modern.

directions.watch_out: Dark interfaces are harder for long text. Offer a light reading mode.
directions.choose_if: images, film or artworks should glow on a dark viewing ground
do: Let artworks and stills carry the color.
avoid: Do not add a second accent hue.
